candidate.title: ChIPmenta- / tion
candidate.scope: The assigned middle Illumina poster row headed “ChIPmenta- / tion,” normalized to ChIPmentation, depicts on-bead Tn5 library preparation of immunoprecipitated chromatin. Its overview caption is “Chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing library preparation by Tn5 transposase (ChIPmentation).” The retained route is Chromatin → Chromatin immunoprecipitation → Adaptor insertion with added Tn5 Transposome → Fragmented and primed → DNA purification / Amplification → DNA. No alternative target workflow, pooling, or retained sample branch is drawn. The left chromatin cartoon illustrates the assay; the neighboring Histone methylation and Chia-PET rows are outside the assigned target. ATAC-seq and purified-DNA ChIP-tagmentation discussed in sources are not additional targets. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete ChIP protocol or a claim that every ChIPmentation implementation shares all upstream preparation.

operations.label: Chromatin immunoprecipitation
operations.description: Select target-associated chromatin from the input using antibody/bead capture, producing bead-bound immunoprecipitated chromatin for tagmentation.
operations.mechanism: Antibody-mediated capture of the chromatin protein or histone modification of interest, retaining its associated DNA on beads.
operations.information_effect: Enriches genomic DNA associated with the chosen antibody target. The target is a protein or protein modification; DNA is the eventual sequencing carrier. Enrichment is antibody-dependent, not a claim of perfect specificity.

operations.label: Adaptor insertion
operations.description: Add the depicted Tn5 transposome to immunoprecipitated, bead-bound chromatin. Tagmentation fragments chromatin DNA and introduces adapter tags, yielding the material summarized as “Fragmented and primed.”
operations.mechanism: Tn5-catalyzed coupled DNA fragmentation and adapter tagging directly on the captured chromatin. The transposome is a catalytic reagent, not a separate chromatin-processing operation.
operations.information_effect: Makes target-enriched genomic fragments compatible with downstream library amplification and sequencing while retaining their genomic sequence as the carrier of the prior ChIP selection.
